rationale: A LIBRARY ANNOTATION is a THIRD annotation position, probed on the pinned grammar: `@TestOn('vm') library annotated.lib;` parses the annotation as a CHILD of `library_name`, BEFORE the dotted library name — unlike the class-level CHILD form (`annotation` inside `class_definition`) and the class-body SIBLING form. The annotated declaration is the library itself, and this lane publishes a module symbol for every file, so the annotation's source is that symbol's name: the DECLARED library name (`annotated.lib`) when the directive has one, else the file-stem convention the module node uses for an implicit/unnamed library. Without this case the library-level annotation published nothing at all: the child-carrier reader had no `library_name` branch, so the type mention never reached the relationship channel.

expectRelationships.note: THE NEW ROW — a library annotation attributes to the module symbol, whose name is the declared library name. `annotatedKind: library_annotation` says the annotated declaration is the library, which no other carrier kind can express.

forbidRelationships.note: THE STEM IS NOT THE SOURCE WHEN A NAME IS DECLARED — this library declares `annotated.lib`, so the module symbol (and therefore the edge source) is that name, not the file stem. A carrier reader that always used the stem would pass the symbol expectation and fail here.
the annotation's ARGUMENT is a value (`'vm'`), not a type — its string literal must not become a row, and it is the reason the target is the `name` field.
an annotation is a TYPE MENTION (`references`), never a value read.
